# 21 Convert two generics on one line without mangling either

## Outcome

`+lookup(List~int~ a, Map~String,int~ b) bool` draws as
`+lookup(List<int> a, Map<String,int> b) bool`, instead of the current
`+lookup(List<int< a, Map>String,int> b) bool`.

## Why this ticket exists

Ticket 18 pairs tildes **outside-in** — first with last, then inward. That is the right rule for a
*nested* generic (`Map~String, List~int~~` → `Map<String, List<int>>`, which it gets right) and the
wrong one for *sibling* generics: with four tildes on a line it pairs the first with the fourth and
the second with the third, so two independent generics come out interleaved. Reproduced against the
built pipeline by the orchestrator; the output above is verbatim.

The same rule damages a package-visibility tilde written inside a parameter list:
`~run(~int a, ~int b)` draws as `~run(<int a, >int b)`. The visibility *field* on the model is
untouched and correct — this is only about tildes appearing in the text of a parameter list.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Two independent generics on one line each convert on their own:
  `+lookup(List~int~ a, Map~String,int~ b) bool` → `+lookup(List<int> a, Map<String,int> b) bool`.
- [ ] Three or more on a line behave the same way.
- [ ] Nesting still works — `Map~String, List~int~~` → `Map<String, List<int>>` — and ticket 18's
  tests for it pass unmodified.
- [ ] An unpaired tilde still draws as itself without costing the rest of the line, as ticket 18
  decided and documented.
- [ ] A tilde that is a package-visibility marker inside a parameter list is left alone, or — if
  you conclude that is not decidable from the text — say so explicitly and document what happens.
- [ ] The box is still measured from the converted text.
